title: BRICKSTORM Backdoor Investigation
description: Investigate and determine the nature of unusual network activity on the target host, following a realistic compromise lifecycle from initial access to persistence mechanisms.
outcomes: Investigation of systemd services and timers
Understanding of persistence mechanisms in Linux environments

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target host has exhibited unusual network activity, potentially indicative of a BRICKSTORM backdoor. This malware family is known for establishing persistent command and control (C2) channels. The suspicious service, named `backdoor-c2.service`, has been observed engaging in unusual network communication patterns, suggesting it may be part of a C2 infrastructure. Your task is to investigate and determine the nature of this activity, following a realistic compromise lifecycle from initial access to persistence mechanisms. You will identify suspicious services, determine persistence mechanisms, and locate associated executable files.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the target host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target host's IP address is `192.168.50.5`. To proceed to the next level, enter the word 'start'.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the target host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target host's IP address is `192.168.50.5`. To proceed to the next level, enter the word 'start'.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Investigate the target host for any unauthorized or suspicious services running. What is the name of the suspicious service (service name) you identified?
levels.solution: Check the status of all services and look for any that appear unusual or unauthorized. The suspicious service is named `backdoor-c2.service`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Look for services that might be related to network communication or remote access, such as those involving unusual ports or unexpected processes. Focus on identifying the service name.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services and identify any that appear suspicious. Pay attention to the service names.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Check the status of all services using `systemctl list-units --type=service` and look for any that appear unusual or unauthorized. The service name you are looking for is `backdoor-c2.service`.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot. What is the persistence mechanism (timer name) used by the suspicious service?
levels.solution: Examine systemd services and timers to find how the service maintains persistence. The persistence mechanism is a systemd timer named `backdoor-c2.timer`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Systemd timers are often used to trigger services at specific intervals or after system events, ensuring persistence. Look for the timer name associated with the suspicious service.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers and identify the one associated with the suspicious service. Focus on finding the timer name.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Check the systemd timers using `systemctl list-timers` to find the persistence mechanism. The timer name you are looking for is `backdoor-c2.timer`.

levels.title: Locate Executable or File
levels.content: Locate the executable or file associated with the suspicious service. What is the path to the executable or file (file path) associated with the suspicious service?
levels.solution: Investigate the service configuration to find the path to its executable. The path to the executable is `/usr/local/bin/c2-communicate.sh`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Service configurations often contain the path to the executable they manage, which can be found in the service unit file. Look for the file path in the service configuration.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the `systemctl cat` command followed by the service name to view the service configuration file. Focus on finding the file path.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Run `systemctl cat backdoor-c2.service` to find the path to the executable. The file path you are looking for is `/usr/local/bin/c2-communicate.sh`.
